name: Klaviyo
tagline: Email, SMS, customer data, automation, analytics, and personalization

pricing.native: Price varies by active profiles and sending volume
pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 250 active profiles, 500 email sends/month, $5 mobile messages/month, 10,000 Composer credits, email support first 60 days.

tiers.name: Marketing paid plan
tiers.limits: Paid by active profiles and message volume; account must fit billable active-profile tier.
tiers.notes: The live build-a-plan table did not expose selected paid quantities clearly enough to store one USD price.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom enterprise terms; numeric caps not published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; 250 active profiles, 500 email sends/month, $5 mobile messages/month, 10,000 Composer credits, email support first 60 days.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly usage/profile-based build-a-plan; no annual discount verified
pricing.hiddenCosts: Active-profile enforcement can move accounts to a higher tier; mobile-message dollars do not roll over; short codes separate; add-ons include Customer Hub from $20/mo, Helpdesk from $10/mo, Customer Agent from $50/mo, Marketing Analytics from $100/mo; Composer credits expire.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Klaviyo's durable value is deliverability, reputation, network, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a small commerce marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: transactional or bulk email provider key in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: sender reputation, deliverability, and suppression handling
whyPeopleStillPay: Klaviyo: The editor is trivial compared with inbox placement, compliance, reputation, unsubscribe handling, analytics, and audience growth infrastructure.
ongoingBurden: Own consent records, suppression lists, bounces, complaints, DNS, templates, accessibility, segmentation, and privacy requests.

priorArt.name: listmonk
priorArt.desc: High-performance self-hosted newsletter and mailing-list manager.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Dittofeed
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent event journeys across email, SMS and push; no ecommerce CDP, predictive personalization or store reporting parity.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mautic
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Automation and segmentation are real; native ecommerce data, SMS economics and predictive analytics are not.

notes: Credibility row: Klaviyo survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Klaviyo; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL.
Primary job: Build a small commerce marketing editor and subscriber database that exports clean HTML and sends only through a reputable user-supplied email provider.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: bounce, complaint, and suppression handling; large-scale segmentation and automation; payments, recommendations, and audience network.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
